note:
The routing REQUEST as it rides on kind:44221 `session.hire`. Brian's ruling of 2026-08-30; the split into request-vs-record is the fix for ledger draft 97, where the CLI emitted the RECORD on a hire and the desktop host accepted only the REQUEST, so every routed hire was classified malformed and dropped in silence.

This file is the one contract three implementations are pinned to: buzz-core's validator (crates/beekeeper-core/src/coding_session_routing.rs, HireRoutingRequest), the CLI's emitter (crates/beekeeper-cli/src/commands/sessions/crew_cmds.rs, cmd_hire) and the desktop host's parser (desktop/src/features/coding-sessions/lib/codingSessionHireRouting.ts). A change here is a change to all three.

THE RULE: the hire carries the QUESTION. `class` and `risk` are required; `profile`, `override`, `challengerSample`, `reviewFlags` and `proposed` are omitted when they have nothing to say — never written as an explicit null. `risk` has THREE keys and no `score`: the product is arithmetic the host does, and a score a requester could set is a number that can disagree with its own factors. `proposed` is the requester's own local decision (what `bee sessions route` computed) and is INFORMATIONAL — it never binds the host, whose live catalog may legitimately differ; when the host lands somewhere else it says so in the record's `proposedDisagreement`.

requests.name: fast builder, no override
requests.why: The ordinary case and the smallest honest shape: a class, a risk triple, and the decision the requester's own router reached. Risk 1x2x2 = 4 lands in the FAST band (1-8), so the requester proposed codex-primary/gpt-5.6-luna at low effort. Nothing optional is written at all.

proposed.reason: codex-primary/gpt-5.6-luna cleared the builder gate (agency>=4.4, coding>=4.2, discipline>=4.5, verification>=4.2) and is the cheapest expected accepted completion at fast/low (2.0 vs 2.5 for codex-primary/gpt-5.4-mini)

requests.name: standard builder with an override and its because
requests.why: A human overruling the router. Risk 3x3x2 = 18 is STANDARD, and the requester's own router proposed claude-primary/sonnet; the human names codex-primary/gpt-5.6-terra instead and must say why. `because` is required by the validator: an unexplained override is indistinguishable from a bug. The hire's top-level `model` is set for this case and only for this case, and equals `override.model`.

override.because: spending this lane's standard builder job on Terra deliberately: it is a challenger for this class (spec 8) and has no measured result yet, and this lane is reversible enough to be the place to buy one

proposed.reason: claude-primary/sonnet cleared the builder gate (agency>=4.4, coding>=4.2, discipline>=4.5, verification>=4.2) and is the cheapest incumbent for builder/standard at medium (2.9); codex-primary/gpt-5.6-luna is cheaper at 2.0 but is unranked for this class and tier, so it holds no route here

requests.name: deep architect with review flags, a profile and a challenger sample
requests.why: Every optional key at once, so a parser that drops one is caught. Risk 5x4x4 = 80 is DEEP; two spec 6 triggers are asserted by name (`contractChange`, `leadRequests`) and they are tokens from REVIEW_FLAG_NAMES, refused by name if unknown rather than dropped. The `profile` raises taste above the architect gate. No `proposed`: a requester with no readable registry has nothing to propose, and that is legal - the host still routes.

rejected.name: the routing RECORD on a hire - exactly the 2026-08-30 09:52 drop
rejected.why: This is what `bee sessions hire` actually put on the wire before this fix, and what the desktop host silently discarded. The validator must refuse it and NAME the offending key, so the answer is `tier belongs to the record` and not a shrug.

routing.reason: claude-primary/sonnet cleared the builder gate and is the cheapest incumbent for builder/standard at medium

rejected.name: a risk that carries its own score
rejected.why: `score` is the record's, not the request's. A requester that can set the product can set one that disagrees with its own factors.
